note: Work-keyed spine for migne.app — ONE record per workIdno; cross-listed dubia/spuria and collection pieces carry multiple attributions (each with its author-level triage status). Column refs follow ORIGINAL Migne plates (via Corpus Corporum TEI <pb> marks), not Garnier reprints. colFirst/colLast null at work level when a work spans volumes (columns restart per tome) — use per-text ranges. colLast is the HIGHEST mark (robust to stray final-pb typos). pbMonotonic=false (~27% of texts) is mostly benign structure, not corruption: bare-number marks step back a column at page-pair boundaries (odd/even columns share a page), and some files interleave parallel versions or appendices — the Phase 5 chunker continuity validator MUST tolerate these patterns, not assume strict ascent. translation.workStatus/englishState await the per-work pass. cpl awaits Clavis enrichment.

translation.note: Sermo de missione Spiritus Sancti — PL 196.1017–32; appears in a Gallica manuscript description alongside other Richard opuscula. Could not confirm in VTT 4 or VTT 8 tables of contents checked. | 2026-07-28: attribution confirmed (see attributionBasis). The does-English-exist check was DELIBERATELY SKIPPED (Wilson) — consistent with the 2026-07-17 untranslated-first relaxation, under which prior English is not disqualifying so long as it is acknowledged openly. englishState therefore stays "unclear" and is honest: we do not know.
translation.attributionBasis: Medieval MS transmission in a homogeneous Richard codex (BnF btv1b10721469k, s. XIII 1/4, ff. 105v-111v, alongside De eruditione interioris hominis, De exterminatione mali, De Emmanuele); listed without a doubtful-attribution asterisk in Feiss, Victorine Texts in Translation 4 abbreviations ("Missione: De missione Spiritus sancti sermo, PL 196.1017-32"); no dissent found in 13 searches. Corpus-wide grep of all 5,276 PL TEI files: six distinctive phrases occur ONLY in 11556.xml, so the sermon is not double-printed under Hugh, Achard, Walter or anonymously — the commonest PL 196 failure mode is absent. NOT a Liber exceptionum extract: the LE sermons were mis-shelved into Hugh's PL 177.901-1210, the opposite direction, and 11556 has no counterpart there. Richard has exactly one sermo in the Corpus Corporum PL index — this one — so there is no block of sermones for a stray piece to have been swept into. NOT closed: Goy's MS repertory (Bibl. Victorina 18), Chatillon's LE intro (TPMA 5) and Ribaillier (TPMA 15) are all paywalled and would settle it. No critical edition of this sermon exists; the attribution has not had a dedicated critical examination. Confidence ~80%.
